# Consensus Without a Central Brain — Ledger of Empty Chairs

## 1. Decoding the problem

Strip the skin off the game terms and this is: **N stateless replicas, no leader, one append-only log, must emit one identical output stream forever.**

- *"Stateless workers"* → a worker is a pure function `step(state, input)`; its only memory is the ledger. Cold start = fold the ledger from the last checkpoint.
- *"Empty chairs"* → the eligible-voter set `E` (the chairs) is itself a ledger-defined roster. No chair is privileged; a chair *empties* when it is struck (fenced). Leadership is a permanently vacant chair.
- *"One honest voice"* → the output stream is the sequence of sealed payloads in chain order. Formal property: at any instant, any two workers' outputs are prefix-comparable (`out_i ⊑ out_j` or vice versa), and all converge to one limit stream σ.
- *"No drift"* → every decision is a **pure function of a ledger prefix**. No wall clocks, no floats, no map-iteration order, no local counters. The chain position **is** the logical clock.

The one structural trick that makes leaderless work: **every validity predicate is prefix-local** — evaluable at a record's own position in the hash chain, identically by every worker, with no side channel. Chain position replaces the coordinator.

---

## 2. Ledger grammar (exact)

Hash chain: each record carries `prev_hash = H(previous record)`. `H = SHA-256`. Canonical encoding: fields sorted by tag, `tag ‖ len_be32 ‖ body`, fixed-width big-endian integers, **no floating point anywhere** (world coordinates are fixed-point, e.g. 1e-6 units). Re-encoding a record must reproduce its bytes bit-for-bit.

Record types:

| Type | Fields |
|---|---|
| `INPUT` | payload_hash, payload |
| `PROPOSE` | slot, round, chair_id, digest |
| `VOTE` | slot, round, chair_id, digest |
| `CHECKPOINT` | height, state_hash, code_version |
| `STRIKE` | chair_id, reason_hash |

**Validity predicates** (evaluated at the record's own chain position `p`; all are prefix-local):

- **V1** `prev_hash == H(prev record)`
- **V2** encoding is canonical
- **V3** for PROPOSE/VOTE: `slot > sealed_height(prefix p)` ∧ `chair_id ∈ E(prefix p)` ∧ no earlier VOTE in the chain by the same chair with the same `(slot, round)`
- **V4** `code_version == pinned_version(prefix p)` (kills version-skew drift)
- **V5** CHECKPOINT: `state_hash == fold(committed payloads ≤ height)` (verifiable lazily; deterministic)

Predicate V3 is the load-bearing one: **a vote is valid only if, at its chain position, the slot was not yet sealed and the chair had not yet voted in that round.** Late votes for a sealed slot self-invalidate. No epochs broadcast, no leases, no leader.

---

## 3. Measured signals (integers read off the ledger — nothing estimated)

| Signal | Definition | Healthy value |
|---|---|---|
| **S1** `votes(p,s,r,d)` | # distinct valid VOTE records at positions ≤ p for (slot s, round r, digest d) | reaches Q, then slot seals |
| **S2** `forks(s,r)` | # distinct digests holding ≥ 1 valid vote in (s,r) | collapses to 1 within ~2 rounds |
| **S3** `participation(s,r)` | # distinct chairs with a valid vote in (s,r) | ≥ Q |
| **S4** `divergence(h)` | # distinct CHECKPOINT `state_hash` values recorded at height h | **exactly 1** — this is the drift meter |
| **S5** `lag(i)` | `sealed_height − applied_height(i)` | bounded by replication delay; liveness only |
| **S6** `gap(i)` | max observed height − local height | 0..small |

S4 is the drift instrument: workers periodically checkpoint their folded state hash at a common height. Identical code + identical prefix ⇒ identical hash. Any S4 > 1 is measured nondeterminism, located to the exact height and the exact deviating chairs.

---

## 4. Closed-form decision rules

**R1 — Quorum (closed form).**
- Crash-fault tolerance: `Q = ⌊N/2⌋ + 1`, tolerates `F = N − Q = ⌈N/2⌉ − 1` failures.
- Byzantine tolerance: `Q = 2F + 1`, requires `N ≥ 3F + 1`. (Check: two quorums intersect in ≥ 2Q − N ≥ F + 1 chairs, at least one honest.)

**R2 — Seal (the commit rule).**
Slot `s` is sealed with digest `d` at chain position
```
p* = min { p : ∃ r, d : votes(p, s, r, d) ≥ Q }
```
Sealing is a *derived fact*, not a record — though an explicit `SEAL` certificate carrying the Q vote hashes may be appended so verification costs O(Q) instead of O(prefix). The payload of `d` enters the voice stream at position `p*`.

**R3 — Vote choice (deterministic winner function).**
```
d*(p,s,r) = argmin_lex { d : votes(p,s,r,d) = max_c votes(p,s,r,c) }
```
Highest valid count; ties broken by byte-wise lexicographic order of the digest. The lex tiebreak is **not cosmetic** — it is the collapse mechanism: on a perfect split, every honest chair computes the same lex-min winner and concentrates on it next round. Guaranteed termination.

If no candidate exists, a chair proposes its own deterministic block: all `INPUT` records since the previous seal, sorted by `(payload_hash, chair_id)` — a canonical cut. Concurrent cuts create forks; the vote resolves them at a cost of one round.

**R4 — Round advance.**
Enter round `r+1` for slot `s` when `participation(s,r) ≥ Q` (S3) and the slot is unsealed, or after timeout `τ(r) = τ₀·2^r + (H(chair_id ‖ s ‖ r) mod W)`. Jitter comes from a hash, not a clock, so behavior stays reproducible. Timeouts gate retries only — **they never select values.**

**R5 — Fencing.**
Any record failing V1–V4 is ignored, and its author's chair is struck via `STRIKE` (itself a sealed decision). Struck chairs leave `E`; their past valid votes stand, their future ones don't.

**R6 — Drift response (honesty rule).**
If `divergence(h) = k > 1`: retain the majority state hash, strike the minority chairs. If no majority exists (k-way split), append `HALT`: the voice goes silent rather than assert anything not derivable from sealed records. **Silence over guessing is the definition of the honest voice here.**

---

## 5. Why this works — the two theorems

**Safety (one voice, zero drift).**
1. Votes are valid only under prefix-local predicates (V3), so every worker evaluates the same valid-vote set.
2. Suppose two distinct digests seal the same `(slot, round)`. Each seal needs Q valid votes, one per chair per round ⇒ 2Q valid votes from ≤ |E| chairs ⇒ 2Q ≤ |E| ⇒ Q ≤ |E|/2 — contradicting `Q = ⌊|E|/2⌋ + 1`. ∎ At most one digest seals per slot.
3. Seals occur at totally ordered chain positions ⇒ the sealed-payload sequence σ is unique. Every honest worker emits σ truncated at its observation frontier; any two outputs are prefix-comparable at all times; all converge to σ. **That is "speaking as one voice," stated as a theorem, not a hope.**

**Liveness.** If ≥ Q chairs are correct and records eventually propagate to all honest chairs: round r achieves participation ≥ Q; if the vote fragments, R4 advances and R3 concentrates all honest mass on the plurality winner — within ≤ 2 rounds of full visibility, its count reaches Q. Common case (identical deterministic proposals): seals in 1 round (propose → attest → sealed). Worst case is bounded, deterministic, and clock-free.

---

## 6. Constants (worked instances)

| N | Fault model | F tolerated | Q | Safety check 2Q ≤ N… wait, Byzantine uses 2Q > N+F |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | crash | 1 | 3 | 2·3=6 > 4+1 ✓ |
| 7 | crash | 3 | 4 | ✓ |
| 7 | Byzantine | 2 | 5 | 10 > 9 ✓ |
| 10 | Byzantine | 3 | 7 | 14 > 13 ✓ |
| 100 | Byzantine | 33 | 67 | 134 > 133 ✓ |

Deployment knobs (correctness-independent): `τ₀ ≈ 200 ms`, jitter window `W ≈ 100 ms`, checkpoint interval `K = 64` slots (cold start folds O(K) records).

---

## 7. Summary of the mechanism in one breath

**The hash chain is the clock. Every rule is a pure function of a prefix. Slot contention is settled by repeated plurality vote with a lex tiebreak, one vote per chair per round, sealed at the earliest prefix where a digest hits Q. Quorum intersection makes double-seals arithmetically impossible; prefix-local validity makes every evaluator agree; checkpointed state hashes measure drift to the bit; and when measurement contradicts assumption, the voice halts instead of lying.** No brain required — the ledger is the brain, and it is empty of occupants by design.
reasoning:
Let me parse this problem carefully.

"Consensus without a central brain: N stateless workers speak as one honest voice, no drift, in the Ledger of Empty Chairs game world."

This is a hard distributed systems problem dressed in game-world language. Let me decode:

- **N stateless workers**: workers with no persistent local state between invocations. They can't accumulate memory. So any "state" must be reconstructed from the ledger each time.
- **Speak as one honest voice**: they must produce identical outputs (deterministic consensus) despite running at different times, on different machines, seeing messages in different orders.
- **No drift**: outputs must not diverge over time — no clock skew, no floating-point divergence, no ordering ambiguity.
- **Ledger of Empty Chairs**: the shared append-only log is the only coordination substrate. "Empty chairs" suggests seats/roles that are currently unoccupied — i.e., leaderless. No designated coordinator. The ledger is the only thing that persists.

So the real engineering question: how do N stateless, leaderless workers reach deterministic agreement using only an append-only log, such that every worker that reads the log computes the *same* next action?

This is essentially: **deterministic state machine replication where the log itself is the source of truth and workers are pure functions of a log prefix**. The classic answer is:

1. Workers are pure functions: `next_action(log_prefix) → action`. Determinism means same prefix → same action.
2. Agreement on *what* to append requires either:
   - A total order on appends (which needs a sequencer — but we have no central brain), or
   - A deterministic tie-break rule that all workers apply identically to whatever they observe.

The hard part without a central brain: two workers may propose conflicting entries concurrently. Without a sequencer, you need either:
- A consensus protocol (Raft/Paxos) — but those elect leaders ("a central brain"), which the problem forbids.
- Leaderless quorum approaches (Dynamo-style) with CRDTs / deterministic merge functions.
- Or: make the merge function commutative, associative, idempotent so order doesn't matter (CRDT semantics), plus a deterministic canonicalization so the "voice" is single.

But wait — "speak as one honest voice" means the output must be a single stream, not a set of divergent streams. And "no drift" means even tiny nondeterminism (hash iteration order, float ops, time) must be eliminated.

Also "measured-not-guessed": give measured signals and closed-form decision rule. So I need to define:
- What signals are measured from the ledger (e.g., per-worker proposal counts, quorum overlap sizes, lag, duplicate rates).
- A closed-form decision rule (an explicit formula/threshold) that decides which entry wins, when to act, when to fence.

Let me design this concretely.

### Model

- Ledger L = append-only sequence of records r_1, r_2, ..., each record: `{seq, worker_id, epoch, payload_hash, payload, prev_hash}` forming a hash chain (prev_hash = H(r_{i-1})). Hash chain gives tamper-evidence and total order once appended.
- Workers are stateless: given (L prefix, input message), they compute deterministically.
- No leader. Any worker can propose by appending a candidate record.
- Problem: concurrent proposals → forks at the tail. Need deterministic resolution.

### Key insight: the ledger's hash chain gives a total order for committed records; the only ambiguity is the uncommitted tail. Resolve the tail with a deterministic, order-independent reduction.

Approach: **Deterministic batch + quorum intersection + hash-chain fencing**.

Actually, let me think about what "measured signals" means. In these Ghost-style problems, you typically want:

1. Define observables you can measure directly from the system (not estimates): e.g., `q = |{workers whose head-hash matches}|` (agreement width), `d = max lag`, fork depth `f`.
2. Closed-form decision rule: e.g., commit iff `q ≥ ⌈(2N+1)/3⌉`... but that's just quorum. To be more interesting and exact, derive it.

Let me build the full mechanism:

#### Mechanism: Two-phase append with deterministic canonicalization

Phase 1 — Propose: worker w, having read ledger up to height h with head hash H_h, appends `PROPOSE(seq=h+1, w, digest=H(payload))`.

Phase 2 — Attest: other workers, upon observing proposals for seq h+1, append `ATTEST(seq=h+1, voter=w, digest_voted)`.

Commit rule: a proposal `(h+1, d)` is committed iff attestation count ≥ Q. But multiple digests can compete for slot h+1. Tie-break must be deterministic and computable by every stateless worker from the ledger alone:

**Closed-form winner rule**: For slot s, let C_s = multiset of distinct proposed digests with their attest counts. Winner = argmax over (attest_count, then lexicographically smallest digest). Formally:

winner(s) = d* where d* = min{ d ∈ D_s : count(d) = max_{d'∈D_s} count(d') }, ties broken by byte-wise lexicographic order of d.

Every worker computing this from the same ledger prefix gets the same answer — that's the "one voice." Determinism holds because the ledger prefix is totally ordered by the hash chain.

But there's still a liveness/consistency subtlety: attestations themselves are appended concurrently; counts change. A worker might see count(d)=Q and commit while another sees a later state where... no — commits are monotone if we require the commit condition to be evaluated against a prefix and the winner rule is stable under appending more records? Not necessarily stable: adding attestations can change the winner. That breaks consistency unless we freeze.

Fix: **epoch/fencing via the hash chain**. Once a digest reaches quorum Q for slot s, the first record that makes it reach Q acts as the commit certificate; everything after must extend from that. Since the ledger is a chain, the commit point is well-defined: the earliest prefix P such that winner(P, s) has count ≥ Q. All workers agree on "earliest prefix reaching quorum" because prefixes are totally ordered. After that, slot s is sealed: any competing proposal for s is ignored (fenced out), and its proposer must re-propose for the next slot derived from the sealed state.

That gives safety. Now the "measured signals":

Signals measurable from the ledger (all exact integers, no estimation):

1. **Agreement width** `A(h)` = size of the largest set of consecutive recent records whose hashes are unanimously observed by independent readers... hmm, actually let me define signals that matter for the decision rule:

- `n_obs(s, d)` = number of ATTEST records for (slot s, digest d) — exact count from ledger scan.
- `fork_depth f` = number of distinct digests competing in the current open slot.
- `stall time` — but time is banned for determinism? Time can be used for liveness (timeouts) as long as it doesn't affect output values, only when to retry. Drift-free output requires time-independence of the decision function; timeouts only gate retries. That's fine and standard.

2. **Quorum bound derivation**: With N workers, tolerate F Byzantine faults → Q = 2F+1 with N ≥ 3F+1 (PBFT-style). Tolerate F crash faults → Q = ⌊N/2⌋+1. Closed form: Q_crash = ⌊N/2⌋ + 1; Q_bft = 2⌊(N−1)/3⌋ + 1.

But maybe the problem wants something more specific to "no drift" — the drift angle suggests numeric determinism: fixed-point arithmetic, canonical serialization (sorted keys, big-endian, length-prefixed), content-addressed payloads, integer-only scoring. The "measured signals" could include drift detectors:

Hmm, let me reconsider the whole framing. "Ledger of Empty Chairs" — empty chairs = roles with no occupant. Maybe the game world has "chairs" (seats/positions) and the workers must agree on who sits where, or the chairs are leadership slots that remain empty (leaderless). The phrase "speak as one honest voice" = single output stream. "No drift" = convergence guarantee.

I think the strongest concrete answer:

**Architecture**: Ledger-as-total-order + pure-function workers + deterministic tail-resolution + quorum sealing + drift detection via state-hash checkpoints.

**Measured signals** (exact, from ledger):

Wait — but if workers are stateless and pure, drift shouldn't happen unless code versions differ. Version pinning: each record carries CODE_VERSION; workers only attest to records with version equal to the version pinned in the genesis/last-seal record. That kills version-skew drift deterministically.

Let me also handle the "one honest voice" emission: the output stream is defined as the sequence of committed payloads in chain order. Every worker emits exactly the committed prefix it has observed; since commits are prefix-monotone, all voices are prefixes of one infinite stream — that's "speaking as one voice" formally: ∀ workers i,j at any time, out_i and out_j satisfy out_i ⊑ out_j or out_j ⊑ out_i (prefix order). No drift = the limit stream is unique.

Now, why does this need no central brain? Because:
- Total order comes from the hash chain (each record commits to its predecessor), not from a sequencer.
- Slot contention resolved by deterministic function of ledger contents, not by a leader.
- Progress guaranteed by quorum intersection: any two quorums share ≥ 1 honest worker (crash model: Q > N/2 ⇒ |Q1∩Q2| ≥ 1; Byzantine: 2Q > N+F ⇒ intersection contains an honest node).

Liveness: with crash faults F and N ≥ 2F+1, at least N−F ≥ Q workers are alive; if they all propose/attest the same digest (because the payload is a deterministic function of the committed prefix + shared input), the first Q attestations seal it. Deterministic proposal: payload for slot s+1 = step(state_s, input_batch_s) where input_batch_s = canonicalized set of client messages that reached ≥ ... hmm, input inclusion also needs agreement. Simplest: inputs enter the ledger as INPUT records; the batch for slot s = all INPUT records between seal(s−1) and the proposal point, canonically sorted by (hash, voter). Different proposers may pick different cut points → different digests → fork → resolved by voting. That's fine; the vote resolves it. To reduce forks: propose only on (a) new input observed, or (b) timeout with empty block. Forks cost one round but resolve deterministically.

Now the "measured-not-guessed" demand: give the actual numbers/formulas:

- Q(N, F_crash) = ⌊N/2⌋ + 1
- Q(N, F_byz) = 2F+1 with constraint N ≥ 3F+1
- Max tolerable simultaneous crash faults for liveness: F < N − Q = N − ⌊N/2⌋ − 1 = ⌈N/2⌉ − 1
- Vote budget: total votes cast per slot ≤ N; sealing consumes Q; slack = N − Q.

No—votes are one-per-slot). Hmm.

Careful: one-vote-per-slot means a worker can't switch its vote. If votes split 40/60 across two digests with Q=51, neither seals. Deadlock! Need vote switching or multi-round slots. Standard fix: allow vote switching (like Raft voting is per-term; here per-slot-round). Introduce round number within slot: ATTEST(slot, round, voter, digest); one vote per (voter, slot, round). Deterministic winner per round; if no digest reaches Q in round k, move to round k+1 where voters attest to the deterministic winner-of-record-so-far (plurality with lex tiebreak). Claim: plurality is monotone non-decreasing across rounds for the leading digest if all honest voters vote for the current plurality leader... Actually with vote switching each round and honest voters all voting for the current plurality winner, the plurality share among honest voters weakly increases each round; once it exceeds F + (something) it seals. Deterministic termination: eventually all honest voters vote for the same digest (the lex-smallest among those with max observed count — converges because once a digest has strict plurality among honest nodes and everyone votes for it, it keeps max count). Participation quorum is clean: if ≥ Q voted in round k and none sealed, everyone will eventually see those Q votes (ledger replication assumption: all records eventually visible to all honest workers — this is the standard eventual-delivery assumption of gossip ledgers). Then all compute the same round-k tally and the same d*, converge. Good — that's deterministic given eventual visibility, no clocks needed for correctness (timeouts only as fallback for liveness).

So final mechanism: **per-slot repeated plurality vote with deterministic lex tie-break, one vote per (voter, slot, round), sealed at earliest prefix where a digest's valid vote count ≥ Q.**

Safety proof (closed-form): two digests sealed in same (slot, round) ⇒ 2Q valid votes from ≤ N voters ⇒ 2Q ≤ N ⇒ Q ≤ N/2, contradicting Q = ⌊N/2⌋+1. Across rounds: sealing in round k freezes the slot; validity rule rejects round-k votes recorded after the seal? Hmm — votes are in a total order; a vote for round k appended after the seal of slot s is still "in round k". Could a second digest reach Q in round k after the first sealed? Yes in principle (late-arriving votes). Fix: validity of a vote depends on the prefix at append time — but stateless workers can't know "append time"... Actually they can: the vote record includes prev_hash; validity rule: a vote is valid iff at its position in the chain, the slot was not yet sealed AND the voter hadn't already voted in (slot, round) earlier in the chain. Since the chain is totally ordered, "not yet sealed at this position" is a deterministic predicate of the prefix ending at that record. So late votes for a sealed slot are automatically invalid. Every worker evaluating validity gets the same answer. Safety holds exactly. This is the crucial trick: **make validity a prefix-local predicate**, so no clocks, no epochs broadcast, no leader — the chain position IS the clock.

Beautiful. That's the core: **the hash-chain position is the logical clock; every decision rule is a pure function of a prefix; seals are prefix-local events.**

Drift elimination checklist (concrete):
1. Canonical encoding: CBOR/RLP-ish with sorted field tags, fixed-width integers, big-endian; hash = SHA-256 over canonical bytes. No floats anywhere in consensus-relevant data; game-world coordinates as fixed-point integers (e.g., 1e-6 units).
2. State hash checkpoints: every K slots, each worker appends CHECKPOINT(height, state_hash). Validity: state_hash must equal the deterministic fold of committed payloads; mismatch ⇒ that worker's future votes invalid (fenced) — deterministic exclusion. Signal: `divergence(h) = |{distinct state_hash at height h}|`; healthy = 1.
3. Code version pinning: VERSION record; votes on records with different version are invalid.
4. No wall-clock in decision functions; timeouts only trigger proposals/retries, never select values. Jitter from H(worker_id‖slot‖round) mod window — reproducible.

Measured signals table (all integers read off the ledger):
- S1 `votes(s,r,d)` — valid vote count. Seal when max_d votes ≥ Q.
- S2 `open_forks(s,r)` = #distinct digests with ≥1 valid vote. Healthy ≤ small; persistent growth ⇒ input asymmetry or Byzantine spam ⇒ escalate round.
- S3 `participation(s,r)` = #distinct voters. Advance round when participation ≥ Q and unsealed.
- S4 `divergence(h)` = #distinct checkpoint state-hashes at height h. Must equal 1; else fence minority / halt if no majority.
- S5 `apply_lag(i)` = sealed_height − applied_height(i). Liveness SLO; no correctness role.
- S6 `chain_gap` = max observed height − local height (replication health).

Decision rules (closed form):
- R1 (quorum): Q = ⌊N/2⌋ + 1 (crash-tolerant); for Byzantine F: Q = 2F+1, require N ≥ 3F+1.
- R2 (seal): slot s sealed with digest d at the earliest chain position p such that votes_prefix(p, s, r_p, d) ≥ Q, where r_p is the round active at p. Emit payload(d) into the voice stream at that position.
- R3 (vote choice): vote for d* = argmax over candidates c of tuple (valid_votes(c), −bytes(c)) i.e., highest count, lex-smallest tiebreak; if no candidates, propose own deterministic block (canonical input cut).
- R4 (round advance): enter round r+1 upon observing participation(s, r) ≥ Q with no seal, or after deterministic timeout τ_r = τ0·2^r (timeout affects liveness only).
- R5 (fence): ignore any record whose validity predicate fails (double vote, post-seal vote, bad prev_hash, wrong version, non-canonical encoding). Fenced workers excluded from tallies permanently (their voter key struck from the eligible set — eligibility set E is itself ledger-defined: E = initial roster minus struck keys; changes to E are themselves sealed decisions).
- R6 (drift response): if divergence(h) = k > 1: keep majority hash (if exists), strike minority workers; if no majority (k-way split with none > |E|/2), emit HALT record — voice goes silent rather than lying (honesty preserved: never guess).

"One voice" formal statement: Let σ = the infinite sequence of sealed payloads in chain order. Every honest worker's emitted stream is σ truncated at its observation frontier. Hence at any moment, any two outputs are comparable by the prefix relation, and as t→∞ all converge to σ. Uniqueness of σ follows from R1+R2 (at most one seal per slot). That's the theorem.

Safety theorem (proof in three lines):

Canonical bytes: `enc(x) = tag || len(x_be32) || body`, fields sorted by tag; integers big-endian two's complement fixed width; no floats; strings UTF-8; H = SHA-256.

Record types:
- PROPOSE {slot, round, proposer, digest, body_hash}
- VOTE {slot, round, voter, digest}
- SEAL is implicit: no seal record needed — seal is a derived fact (earliest prefix where count ≥ Q). But emitting an explicit SEAL record helps cheap verification: SEAL {slot, round, digest, cert_hashes[Q]} — verifiable in O(Q) instead of O(prefix). Optional optimization; mention.
- CHECKPOINT {height, state_hash, version}
- STRIKE {chair, reason_hash} — removes eligibility.
- INPUT {payload_hash, payload}

Validity predicates (prefix-local, evaluated at the record's own chain position p):
V1: prev_hash == H(previous record)
V2: enc is canonical (re-encoding equals bytes)
V3: PROPOSE/VOTE: slot > sealed_height(prefix p) ; voter/proposer ∈ E(prefix p); no earlier VOTE by same voter with same (slot, round)
V4: version(record) == pinned_version(prefix p)
V5: CHECKPOINT.state_hash == fold(committed payloads up to height) — expensive; verify lazily/sampled, but deterministic.

Tally function: votes(p, s, r, d) = |{distinct valid VOTE records at positions ≤ p with (s, r, d)}|.

Seal: slot s sealed at position p* = min{ p : ∃d, r : votes(p, s, r, d) ≥ Q }. Voice appends payload(d) at p*.

Winner rule R3 exact: d*(p, s, r) = argmin over { d : votes(p,s,r,d) = max_c votes(p,s,r,c) } by byte-wise lexicographic order of d. (argmin lex = deterministic.)

State fold: state_{s+1} = Step(state_s, canonical_input_cut(s)); canonical_input_cut(s) = sort by (H, proposer) of all INPUT records in (pos(seal s−1), pos(proposal)] — but cut differs per proposer; that's why forks happen; resolved by vote. Fine.

Backoff/jitter: sleep_jitter = H(chair_id ‖ s ‖ r) mod W; timeout τ(s,r) = τ0 · 2^r + jitter. Only liveness.
